title: Microsoft buys ~600 acres in Woodward Eco Business Park for a data center campus; residents' meeting Oct 12
summary: Microsoft disclosed a roughly 600-acre land purchase in the Woodward Eco Business Park, near Des Moines. At a residents' meeting on Oct 12, 2026 (held after the council's regular meeting was canceled), a resident asked whether residents could vote on the project; the mayor answered no. Microsoft says the project is at its earliest planning phase.
source_title: Newsweek — Man dragged from Iowa meeting protesting Microsoft data center
verbatim: Microsoft has purchased land in Woodward for the purpose of datacenter development. This project is at the earliest phase of planning and development and we look forward to working with local leaders and community members as our plans move forward.

Acreage 'about 600 acres' verbatim: 'Microsoft has purchased about 600 acres of land zoned for industrial use in the Woodward Eco Business Park.' DCD page returned 403 to WebFetch; not verified there. Woodward IA is not in the index. Newsweek says the confrontation was at Woodward-Granger High School auditorium. Rezoning from agricultural to Eco Business Park (June 2026) reported in a search snippet only, not verified on a fetched page, so omitted. title: Van Buren Township Planning Commission approves final site plan for Google-owned 282-acre data center campus
summary: The Van Buren Township Planning Commission voted 5-1 on Wednesday, Oct. 14, 2026, to approve a final site plan for the 282-acre campus. Michigan Public reports the site is already zoned for industrial use and that Google will be the final owner and operator. The article does not state MW capacity; 1 GW is from a separate outlet's report and is not verified on the cited page.

title: Oracle voluntarily drops Ozaukee County suit against Wisconsin PSC data center credit-rating rules

facts.rule: A- credit rating threshold for We Energies data center customers; below-threshold firms post cash or credit line collateral

summary: Oracle moved to voluntarily drop its lawsuit against Wisconsin's utility regulator on Monday, Aug. 17, 2026. The suit challenged the PSC's A- credit threshold for data center operators, and Oracle said the requirement could cost it over $100 million per year.
source_title: Wisconsin Watch — Oracle drops lawsuit challenging Wisconsin data center credit rules
